hints: Start by working out what the two possible carbonyl isomers with formula C3H6O must be.
Remember that one isomer is an aldehyde and the other is a ketone, so think about how easily each is oxidised.
Check each of the three reagents in turn for aldehyde versus ketone behaviour, and also for the special methyl-carbonyl group needed for the iodoform test.
walkthrough:
**Identify the two compounds**

Great start, let's see what C3H6O can be. As carbonyl compounds, they must contain C=O.

The only two possibilities are propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ (an aldehyde) and propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ (a ketone).

**Recall aldehyde vs ketone oxidisability**

Here is the key idea. Aldehydes are easily oxidised to carboxylic acids, but ketones resist oxidation because breaking a C-C bond would be needed.

So any mild or strong oxidising agent that oxidises the aldehyde but not the ketone will give a different observation.

**Test reagent 1 - acidified KMnO4**

Acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ is a strong oxidiser, purple in colour.
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + [O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$
Propanal decolourises the purple solution to colourless $\text{Mn}^{2+}$. Propanone shows no change and stays purple. So 1 gives different observations.

**Test reagent 2 - Fehling's reagent**

Fehling's is a mild oxidiser, blue solution containing $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ complex.
$$\text{RCHO} + 2\text{Cu}^{2+} + 5\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{RCOO}^- + \text{Cu}_2\text{O} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Propanal gives a brick-red precipitate of $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ on warming. Propanone gives no change, stays blue. So 2 gives different observations.

**Test reagent 3 - alkaline aqueous iodine**

This is the iodoform test for the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group. It gives a yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$.

Propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, contains this group so gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$. Propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, does not contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ so stays a brown solution with no precipitate. So 3 also gives different observations.

**Conclude the combination**

Since 1, 2 and 3 all distinguish propanal from propanone, the correct combination includes all three.

options.A: Correct. All three reagents distinguish the aldehyde from the ketone. Reagents 1 and 2 rely on easy oxidation of propanal only, and reagent 3 relies on the CH3CO group present only in propanone.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only 1 and 2. Students choose this by correctly spotting the oxidation tests but forgetting that the iodoform test also distinguishes them because only propanone has the CH3CO group.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes only 2 and 3. Students choose this by thinking acidified manganate(VII) is so strong it oxidises both aldehyde and ketone, but ketones resist even strong oxidation under these conditions.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only 1. Students choose this by confusing Fehling's and iodoform conditions, or by thinking both C3 carbonyls give the same result with mild oxidisers. In fact Fehling's is specific to aldehydes and iodoform is specific to methyl ketones here.
